title: Chargers Edge Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night Football for First 2026 Victory – NBC Sports
body:
Los Angeles secured its first victory of the 2026 NFL season on Monday night, edging the Baltimore Ravens 23‑20 in a tightly contested battle that hinged on a dominant ground game and a clutch fourth‑quarter drive. The Chargers amassed 160 rushing yards, dwarfing Baltimore’s 16, and forced a decisive turnover that set up the game‑winning field goal. The win snapped a 0‑3 start for the Chargers and gave rookie quarterback Jacoby Brissett his first chance to prove himself in a starting role for the Ravens, though a late fumble by wideout Zay Flowers proved costly.

From the opening kickoff, Los Angeles imposed its physical style, pounding the Ravens’ defensive front with a mix of inside runs and play‑action passes. Running back Austin Ekeler led the charge, carving up the field for 112 yards and a crucial 27‑yard touchdown in the second quarter that put the Chargers ahead 14‑7. Baltimore answered with a short touchdown pass from Brissett to tight end Mark Andrews, but the Chargers quickly reclaimed the lead after a 45‑yard drive capped by a field goal from Cameron Dicker. By halftime, the scoreboard read 17‑10 in favor of Los Angeles, a margin that reflected the Chargers’ ability to control the line of scrimmage while the Ravens struggled to establish a consistent rushing attack.

The second half saw the Ravens attempt a comeback, relying heavily on Brissett’s arm. The rookie completed 18 of 28 passes for 215 yards, connecting on a 31‑yard strike to Rashod Bateman that set up a field goal, narrowing the gap to 17‑13. However, Baltimore’s offensive rhythm stalled when Flowers, who had been a reliable target throughout the night, was stripped of the ball after a hard hit by defensive end Tarheeb Still. Chargers safety Eric Molden recovered the loose ball at the Ravens’ 38‑yard line, instantly shifting momentum. On the very next play, Los Angeles capitalized with a 12‑yard touchdown pass from quarterback Justin Herbert to Keenan Allen, extending the lead to 23‑13.

The Ravens responded with a late drive that showcased Brissett’s poise under pressure. He orchestrated a 75‑yard march, highlighted by a 22‑yard scramble that kept the drive alive after a sack. The effort culminated in a 33‑yard field goal by Justin Tucker, pulling Baltimore within seven points with just over two minutes remaining. Yet the Chargers’ defense, anchored by veteran linebacker Kyler Fackrell, held firm, forcing a three‑and‑out and giving the offense one final chance.

Herbert, who had been quiet for much of the game, guided the Chargers into field goal range with a series of short, precise passes. Kicker Cameron Dicker nailed a 48‑yard attempt as time expired, sealing a 23‑20 victory. The win not only halted the Chargers’ early-season slide but also underscored the importance of a balanced attack and opportunistic defense in close contests.

Looking ahead, Los Angeles will aim to build on this momentum as it travels to face the Denver Broncos next week, hoping to sustain its rushing dominance while tightening up pass protection. For Baltimore, the loss highlights lingering issues in ball security and the need for a more effective ground game to complement Brissett’s promising arm. Both teams have clear areas to address, and the outcomes of their upcoming matchups could shape the trajectory of their 2026 campaigns.
